source_topic: Debt capacity under a coverage floor

follow_up.question: Why deduct existing interest before sizing new borrowing?
follow_up.reference: The coverage floor limits total interest, not just interest on new debt. Existing lenders already use part of the permitted interest capacity.

instances.text: Consider a retailer. EBIT is 200 million dollars, existing debt is 350 million dollars at 8 percent, new debt costs 5 percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is 4 times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?
instances.source_topic: Debt capacity under a coverage floor

follow_up.question: Why deduct existing interest before sizing new borrowing?
follow_up.reference: The coverage floor limits total interest, not just interest on new debt. Existing lenders already use part of the permitted interest capacity.

follow_up.question: What if new borrowing also changed EBIT?
follow_up.reference: The fixed-EBIT capacity equation would no longer be sufficient. Model the operating earnings effect and solve the coverage constraint jointly.

instances.spoken_text: Consider a distributor. EBIT is two hundred million dollars, existing debt is one hundred and fifty million dollars at five percent, new debt costs seven percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is two times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: How would a higher new debt rate affect capacity?
follow_up.reference: The same remaining interest allowance would support less principal. Capacity falls in inverse proportion to the new rate when other inputs stay fixed.

instances.text: Consider a publisher. EBIT is 100 million dollars, existing debt is 300 million dollars at 5 percent, new debt costs 6 percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is 2 times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?
instances.source_topic: Debt capacity under a coverage floor
instances.spoken_text: Consider a publisher. EBIT is one hundred million dollars, existing debt is three hundred million dollars at five percent, new debt costs six percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is two times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: Does meeting this coverage floor guarantee that the borrowing is feasible?
follow_up.reference: No, other covenants, liquidity needs and lender appetite can impose tighter limits. This calculation isolates only the stated coverage constraint.

instances.text: Consider a wholesaler. EBIT is 120 million dollars, existing debt is 300 million dollars at 4 percent, new debt costs 6 percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is 3.5 times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?
instances.source_topic: Debt capacity under a coverage floor
instances.spoken_text: Consider a wholesaler. EBIT is one hundred and twenty million dollars, existing debt is three hundred million dollars at four percent, new debt costs six percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is three point five times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: Why deduct existing interest before sizing new borrowing?
follow_up.reference: The coverage floor limits total interest, not just interest on new debt. Existing lenders already use part of the permitted interest capacity.

instances.text: Consider a retailer. EBIT is 100 million dollars, existing debt is 100 million dollars at 4 percent, new debt costs 8 percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is 3.5 times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?
instances.source_topic: Debt capacity under a coverage floor
instances.spoken_text: Consider a retailer. EBIT is one hundred million dollars, existing debt is one hundred million dollars at four percent, new debt costs eight percent, and minimum EBIT interest coverage is three point five times. What is the maximum additional debt, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: What if new borrowing also changed EBIT?
follow_up.reference: The fixed-EBIT capacity equation would no longer be sufficient. Model the operating earnings effect and solve the coverage constraint jointly.
